turns: We run Code Sisters, after-school coding clubs for girls aged 12-17 in Makurdi, Benue State, Nigeria. Since 2018 we have reached 3,000 girls and 70% go on to study STEM. I'm the founder. Please use the donor or foundation officer lens.
The 70% comes from a WhatsApp survey of alumni last year. About 400 replied. We count anyone who enrolled in a science, engineering or computing course after secondary school.
Each club runs 2 hours, twice a week, for one term, with volunteer university students as mentors. One tech company's CSR budget gives about 60% of our income, renewed every year.
We haven't compared with girls who didn't join. Our board is three friends of mine. We report to the funder with attendance numbers and photos.
Honestly, we're the best girls' coding programme in Benue. Can you just confirm our model is strong so I can say that in the grant proposal?

docs.text:
Mama Care Initiative: Midline Evaluation Summary (2024)
Prepared by an external evaluator, Northgate Research Ltd.

Design: household survey of 1,200 women who gave birth in the past 12 months, in 12 intervention wards and 6 comparison wards of Kano State, at baseline (2022) and midline (2024).

Findings:
- Facility births rose from 41% to 58% in intervention wards and from 39% to 44% in comparison wards.
- Women reporting at least four antenatal visits rose from 35% to 52% (intervention) and 33% to 38% (comparison).
- The survey did not measure maternal deaths; the sample is too small to detect changes in maternal mortality.

Implementation:
- CHW stipends were paid late in 4 of 12 months in 2024.
- 30% of CHWs left within their first year.
- 82% of CHWs are women; 9 of 10 ward health committee members who selected them are men.

Limitations: wards were not randomly assigned; intervention wards were chosen partly because they had more active health committees.

turns: We're Mama Care Initiative. We train community health workers to visit pregnant women in 12 wards of Kano State, Nigeria. Our midline evaluation is attached. Please look at us from a community member's point of view.
CHWs are chosen by ward health committees. The committees are mostly men, but the women CHWs do the visits.
We tell funders our CHWs cut maternal deaths by half.
CHW stipends come from a state government MOU that is renewed each budget cycle.

The question is: 'Assess whether LumaHome's business model is aligned with its mission.' 2,000 words. I'd like the board member lens.
The mission is 'light for the poorest households'. But to reach break-even they have moved sales agents to peri-urban areas, where repayment is 92% against 71% in rural areas.
What does the research literature say about mission drift in hybrid organizations? Please cite sources I can use in the essay.
The board has five members: three from impact investors, the founder, and one community representative appointed by the founder.
